newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Bankers Trust unit eyes major Argentine loan share.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust unit eyes major Argentine loan share.

text.p: Banco Liniers Sudamericano SA (BLS) said Tuesday a capital increase from an association with a company controlled by Bankers Trust Co, will help it in its bid to become one of Argentina's leading consumer credit lenders.
"After this deal the bank will strenghten its strategy of specializing in this market," Claudio Porcel, BLS's finance and retail banking manager, told Reuters.
"This will allow us all the necessary capital to become one of Argentina's leading consumer credit granters," he added in a phone interview.
Porcel's comments came after the bank announced Monday that Bankers Trust unit BLTA Holdings LLC has signed a deal to buy a 51 percent stake in it in the form of a capital increase.
He declined to disclose the amount of the deal, which has yet to be approved by Argentina's central bank.
Porcel said after the capital increase, current shareholders Alejandro Laurence, Luis Posse, Nestor Porcel and Manuel Rodriguez will together continue to hold 49 percent.
BLS said Monday Laurence and Posse will remain in charge of the management and strategic development of the bank as president and vice president, respectively.

Porcel said BLS was three years ago in talks with General Electric Capital Services, a unit of General Electric, but that negotiations collapsed when BLS's shareholders realized the U.S. firm wanted merely to buy a stake rather than forge an association.t
Porcel said the bank's strategy to become a major player in the consumer credit market will include a future expansion into home mortgage loans and leasing.
"We will analyze the markert. The leasing has many applications."
BLS's main business are credit cards and car loans. It issues Mastercard, Argencard and Visa credit cards.
Porcel said the Buenos Aires-based bank has issued 90,000 credit cards. It has $122 million in assets, $105 million in liabilities and about $100 million in deposits, he added.
